## Security: Node.js runtime advisories (October 2026)

On October 20, 2026, eMudhra disclosed that the private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates could be recovered from the public certificates. On October 21, Node.js shipped [security releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases) that update its bundled CA certificates for the compromise. The same releases fix several unrelated high-severity runtime CVEs, including DNS name truncation, TLS hostname checks on non-canonical IP addresses, and an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder.

**How this release stands**

- **The Inspector relies on the Node.js runtime for certificate checks.** It ships no CA certificates of its own and doesn't opt into the system trust store. Every HTTPS connection it makes, to MCP servers and to OAuth discovery and token endpoints, is verified by the Node.js it runs on.
- **The Docker image needs no action.** `ghcr.io/modelcontextprotocol/inspector:2.13.0` runs Node.js **22.23.4**, a patched release, and contains no system CA store.
- **This release also updates two of its own dependencies past published advisories:** `undici` (#2812) and `fast-uri` (#2820).

**If you run the Inspector from npm (`npx` or a global install)**

It runs on your Node.js, which we can't update for you. Please run Node.js **22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or later**, and check with `node --version`. The package's `engines` field still accepts Node.js 22.19.0 and up, so npm won't warn you about an older, unpatched runtime. Node.js 20 and earlier are end-of-life, get no fix, and aren't supported by Inspector v2.

## What's Changed

### Security fixes

2.12.0 fixes three vulnerabilities that affect every v2 release from 2.0.0 through 2.11.0. Upgrade with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest`.

* **Opening a URL is restricted to `http(s)`, and the Inspector opens the URL it checked rather than the raw input.** A remote server's OAuth authorization URL can no longer run commands through the opener on Windows and WSL. `open` is bumped to v11 ([GHSA-q978-78c7-phqw](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-q978-78c7-phqw))
* **The production web server validates the `Host` header** and answers any host outside its allow-list with 403 before serving a page. That closes the DNS-rebinding route to the API token and stored OAuth tokens. A new `MCP_INSPECTOR_ALLOWED_HOSTS` covers reverse proxies that rewrite `Host` ([GHSA-vcc9-3xgm-p9v4](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-vcc9-3xgm-p9v4))
* **The `/api/fetch` proxy caps upstream response bodies at 4 MiB**, refusing early when `Content-Length` declares more, and still relays the status of an oversized error response ([GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp))

## What's Changed

### v1.x security fixes

1.0.3 is a security release for the deprecated v1 line. Upgrade with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@v1-latest`, or move to v2 (`@latest`).

* **Proxy rejects browser requests without an allowed Origin when authentication is disabled**, and `DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH` is read strictly (only `true`, `1` or `yes`) ([GHSA-wmjf-2m46-2352](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-wmjf-2m46-2352))
* **The OAuth callback no longer takes connection settings from its URL.** It reconnects only with the connection saved in that tab before the redirect, and never over stdio ([GHSA-4fc4-wcmh-4g86](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-4fc4-wcmh-4g86))
* **MCP App links open with `noopener,noreferrer`** and only for http(s) URLs, and the proxy rejects same-origin browser requests to its API. A new `DANGEROUSLY_ALLOW_SAME_ORIGIN_API` opt-out covers single-origin reverse-proxy setups ([GHSA-6x67-4w4w-9f3w](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-6x67-4w4w-9f3w))
* **The stored proxy token is no longer sent to a proxy address supplied in the URL**, and a query-supplied address is no longer saved. `MCP_PROXY_PORT` must be a number ([GHSA-2rq8-f55p-j2jp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-2rq8-f55p-j2jp))
* **The `/fetch` proxy drops `Authorization`, `Cookie` and related headers on cross-origin redirects**, and refuses a cross-origin redirect of a request that still carries a body ([GHSA-f6mc-jg3x-vq53](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-f6mc-jg3x-vq53))
* **The `/fetch` proxy caps upstream response bodies at 5 MiB** ([GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp))
* **SSE connection logs show header names, not values**, and stdio `env` values are masked in the query log ([GHSA-8qgq-27v6-55w3](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-8qgq-27v6-55w3))
* chore: bump version to 1.0.3 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/2754

### New configuration

* `DANGEROUSLY_ALLOW_SAME_ORIGIN_API`: off by default. Set it to `true`, `1` or `yes` only if the client and proxy are served from one origin behind a reverse proxy. See the README's "Same-origin API Requests" section.

## Why The Patch?
The addition of the new `mcpdo` client threw a curveball into the default `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest` method of running the inspector, because there were now two binaries to run, the `launcher` (used by the other clients) and `mcpdo`. This quick follow-up patch restores sanity so that command works again. Instructions for launching new `mcpdo` client are on `README.md`.

## Known issue

**OAuth profiles that share a server can overwrite each other's tokens** ([#2549](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/issues/2549)). If you use `MCP_INSPECTOR_OAUTH_STATE_PATH` to keep separate OAuth profiles against the same server, give each profile its own secret store too: set `MCP_INSPECTOR_SECRET_STORE=file` and a distinct `MCP_INSPECTOR_SECRET_FILE` per profile (or a per-profile `MCP_STORAGE_DIR`). The default single-profile setup is unaffected. A fix is planned for 2.10.0.

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector          # web UI

```

## What's new

v2 ships as a single package with three clients — a Vite + React + Mantine web UI, a scriptable CLI, and an Ink-based TUI — over a shared `@inspector/core` runtime, so all three behave identically.

## Upgrading from v1

- **Node >= 22.19.0** is now required (was >= 22.7.5).
- CLI flags changed substantially. In particular `--config` now means a **read-only session file**; `--catalog` is the writable server list. See [MCP server configuration](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/blob/main/docs/mcp-server-configuration.md).
- The v1 sub-packages (`inspector-client`, `inspector-server`, `inspector-cli`) are deprecated and not part of v2 — v2 publishes a single package.

## v1

v1 is deprecated and receives security fixes only, published under the `v1-latest` tag:

```bash
npm i @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@v1-latest
```
